liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (3 reviews): Slow to get going, but it builds into a spine-chilling version; Reviewer finds this opener sweet [11][14][17]
- **Playin' In The Band** (2 reviews): Reviewer counts this Playin' among their all-time favorites; Nice jamming around the seven-and-a-half-minute mark of the first Playin' [12][22]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review): The Around And Around > Johnny B. Goode > U.S. Blues finale is rousing [14]
- **Lazy Lightnin'** (1 review): The Lazy Lightnin' > Supplication pairing is called sloppy [17]
- **Althea** (1 review): Jerry sounds very relaxed and loose on this Althea [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-03-02 s1 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-02 s1 t02 Shakedown Street**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-02 s1 t03 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-02 s1 t04 Dire Wolf**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-02 s1 t05 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-02 s1 t06 Althea**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-02 s1 t07 El Paso**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd81-03-02 s1 t08 Jack-A-Roe**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-03-02.139734.fob.nak700.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 146 min [1]
- **gd1981-03-02.175076.sbd.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: soundboard; 22 songs; 154 min [4]
- **gd81-03-02.wagner.munder.9511.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 154 min; rated 3.94/5 by 17 [5]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has an immersive feel, as if the listener is surrounded by the music; Reviewer finds the band thin-sounding and the recording quality only so-so; Taped by Bob Wagner without real cuts; sound is close up and favors Phil over Brent [13][16][17][18][19]
- **gd1981-03-02.nak700.wagner.miller.90450.sbeok.flac24**: source not stated; 22 songs; 156 min; rated 4.18/5 by 11 [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer bought tickets on sale day and sat in the first row of the balcony [14]
- Reviewer's first show, seen from third row center at Cleveland Music Hall [19]
- Reviewer's mother attended while pregnant with them, dancing around during the show [20]
- Reviewer has heard much better shows and suggests skipping this one unless completing a collection [16]
- Reviewer rates this night well above the second night in Cleveland [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-03-02.139734.fob.nak700.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master FOB Audience Cassette; Nakamichi CM-700 > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell MX90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi CR-7A) >… [1]. Also: Patches from the motb nak700 source cover the end of Althea, the tuning gap, and the start of El Paso [1]
- **gd1981-03-02.175076.sbd.miller.phase-repair.flac1644**: transferred by DAT Supplied By Rob Eaton Transferred By Digitalrbb Mastered By Charlie Miller  November 10, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Reel > DAT (48k) [4]. Also: Vocal phase problem on shnid 112748 was repaired, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [4]
- **gd81-03-02.wagner.munder.9511.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bob Wagner; source: Audience Recording: Nak 700's [5]
- **gd1981-03-02.nak700.wagner.miller.90450.sbeok.flac24**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 (With Bass EQ) -> Cassette Master (Sony D5M/Maxell DXLIIS/Dolby B) D [6]. Also: A 16-bit version of the same source also circulates [6]
